head: A chip factory
with no chips of its own.
slides.sub: How TSMC built an empire by refusing to compete with its customers.

image.label: A glowing cleanroom seen through a glass wall
image.brief: 유리벽 너머로 보이는 반도체 클린룸. 노란 조명 아래 방진복 차림의 작업자 실루엣. 얼굴은 보이지 않게. 로고 없음.

head: To sell chips,
you had to build a fab.
body: In the early 1980s, chip companies designed their chips and made them in their own factories, called fabs.
A fab cost a fortune and grew outdated fast. Talented engineers with a good design but no factory had almost nowhere to go.

image.label: A 1980s engineer sketching a circuit at a desk
image.brief: 1980년대 사무실에서 회로도를 그리는 엔지니어의 뒷모습. 형광등, 종이 도면, 오래된 컴퓨터 단말기.

head: Taiwan had skilled hands,
not famous designs.
body: In 1985, Taiwan's government invited Morris Chang, who had spent more than 20 years at Texas Instruments, to lead its industrial research institute.
His task: build a chip industry in a country with few chip designers and no global brands.

image.label: Hsinchu streets and new industrial buildings in the 1980s
image.brief: 1980년대 대만 신주의 거리와 새로 짓는 공업 단지 건물. 스쿠터, 습한 공기, 저녁 빛. 실존 인물 얼굴 없음.

head: You can build one fab.
What is it for?
body: Your country can fund a modern chip factory. Global giants already design and sell the best chips.

options.text: Make only other companies' designs, and never sell chips of your own
options.feedback: You give up the profits of owning a product, and few customers exist yet. Keep swiping.

options.text: Design and sell your own chips, like the big companies do
options.feedback: This is the usual path, but you would face rivals with bigger labs and brands. Keep swiping.

options.text: Mass-produce standard memory chips and win on cost
options.feedback: Volume is real, but memory prices swing wildly and rivals are deep-pocketed. Keep swiping.

image.label: An empty plot of land with a fab blueprint on a table
image.brief: 빈 부지를 내려다보는 책상 위에 공장 설계도가 펼쳐진 장면. 1980년대 분위기.

slides.label: chips TSMC designed to sell under its own name
body: TSMC was founded in 1987 with backing from Taiwan's government and Philips. It would only manufacture. Customers could hand over their best designs without fearing TSMC would become a rival.

image.label: A silicon wafer with blank, unbranded chips
image.brief: 브랜드 표시 없는 칩들이 격자로 놓인 실리콘 웨이퍼 클로즈업. 차가운 푸른 빛.

head: At first, customers
treated it as backup.
body: Big chipmakers sent TSMC overflow work their own fabs couldn't handle. A story often told is that one major customer audited the factory closely before trusting it.
TSMC fixed every gap. Each passed audit made the next customer easier to win.

image.label: Inspectors with clipboards walking a factory corridor
image.brief: 클립보드를 든 점검단이 공장 복도를 걷는 장면. 얼굴은 보이지 않는 뒷모습.

head: Then a new kind of company
appeared: no factory.
body: Now a small team could start a chip company with just designs and pay TSMC to make them. These "fabless" firms multiplied in the 1990s.
Graphics chip startups such as Nvidia, founded in 1993, came to rely on TSMC.

image.label: A small startup office with chip boards on the desks
image.brief: 1990년대 작은 스타트업 사무실. 책상 위 회로 기판과 모니터, 밤늦게 일하는 사람들의 실루엣. 로고 없음.

head: Every customer's order
paid for the next fab.
body: Because TSMC served many customers, its factories stayed busy and it could keep building newer ones. TSMC listed in Taiwan in 1994 and in New York in 1997.
By 2000, it was the world's largest dedicated chip foundry.

image.label: Several fab buildings lit up at night
image.brief: 밤에 불 밝힌 여러 동의 반도체 공장 단지. 1990년대 후반 대만 풍경.

head: The promise not to compete
was the product.
body: Big chipmakers couldn't copy TSMC without giving up their own chips. That is counter-positioning.
Saying no to designing chips earned customers' trust. Their combined volume gave TSMC a scale no single customer could match.

image.label: Many small arrows flowing into one factory
image.brief: 여러 방향의 작은 화살표들이 하나의 공장으로 모이는 단순한 그래픽.

head: Sometimes what you refuse
is what you sell.
body: Customers share more, and stay longer, with a partner who will never become their rival.
**Try it today:** is there something you could promise never to do that would make customers trust you more?

image.label: A single wafer glowing on a dark background
image.brief: 어두운 배경 위에서 은은하게 빛나는 웨이퍼 한 장.

factChecks.note: TSMC 설립(1987년, 신주과학단지)과 대만 정부·Philips 공동 출자는 TSMC 공식 연혁 기준입니다. 지분율은 자료마다 달라 카드에 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1987년 대만 정부 개발기금(48.3%)·Philips(27.5%)·민간 출자로 설립 확인.
Morris Chang이 Texas Instruments에서 20년 넘게 일했고, 1985년 대만 정부 초청으로 ITRI 원장을 맡았다는 내용은 TSMC 연혁과 주요 전기 자료로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] Morris Chang의 ITRI 원장 취임 확인(1985년·1986년으로 자료마다 다름).
TSMC가 자체 설계 칩을 만들어 팔지 않는 '순수 파운드리' 모델로 시작했다는 점은 회사 설명 기준입니다. 카드의 '0'은 자체 브랜드 칩 판매가 없다는 의미로만 썼습니다.
초기에 대형 칩 회사가 TSMC 공장을 심사한 일화(흔히 Intel 인증 이야기로 전해짐)는 'a story often told'로 처리하고 회사명을 넣지 않았습니다. 원 출처를 확인하세요.
Nvidia(1993년 설립)가 1990년대 후반부터 TSMC 고객이 되었다는 점은 양사 발언과 보도로 확인하세요.
대만증권거래소 상장(1994년)과 NYSE ADR 상장(1997년)은 TSMC 공식 연혁 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1994년 대만, 1997년 NYSE 상장은 이번 검색에서 미확인.
2000년 무렵 세계 최대 전문 파운드리였다는 표현은 업계 보도 기준입니다. 점유율 수치는 넣지 않았습니다.
